clinician.final_diagnosis: invasive moderate to focally poorly differentiated basaloid squamous cell carcinoma with focal keratinisation
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 54-year-old male smoker presented with localized tenderness and swelling of his left wrist, attributed to a dog bite. Initial investigations showed raised inflammatory markers and a 'normal' wrist X-ray. He was treated with antibiotics for suspected soft tissue infection, with initial improvement, but symptoms recurred after cessation. An MRI of the left wrist revealed an inflammatory mass (30x21mm) centered on the hamate with extensive marrow abnormality. An open surgical exploration and washout of the wrist was performed, draining purulent and gelatinous tissue, which intraoperatively appeared consistent with deep infection. Tissue samples were taken for microbiology and histology. Histology confirmed invasive moderate to focally poorly differentiated basaloid squamous cell carcinoma with focal keratinisation in the wrist. Microbiological cultures from the surgical samples did not isolate any organisms, ruling out bacterial infection. Subsequently, the patient was diagnosed with metastatic lung carcinoma and referred to respiratory specialists, indicating the wrist lesion was a metastasis from a primary lung cancer.
